extracted.intended_audience: data journalists, newsroom editors, and communications/PR professionals who draft data-driven press releases (especially at research institutes)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for creating press releases that present data so that they are picked up by data journalists and mainstream media. Covers data quality, methodological transparency, narrative framing, and multimedia/visualization packaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original/proprietary data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press releases that present original or proprietary datasets are more likely to be picked up than reports that simply repeat existing findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical significance noted
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistically significant findings / statistical significance noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flagging whether results reach statistical significance helps journalists judge newsworthiness; include p-values or tests where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visualizable findings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer results that can be rendered clearly as a chart, map, or infographic — visualization often drives pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear narrative / story with the data
rubrics_metrics.description: Tells a clear story with the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The data should connect to a clear, newsworthy narrative; the release should surface the story rather than bury it in method or tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodologically transparent / Methodology section present / Methodology document linked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a methodology section, link to a full methods document, and consider a methodology infographic. Transparency about how data were collected and analyzed is essential for credibility and reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison points provided
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide comparative context — yoy, peer groups, or baseline comparisons — to make the magnitude and direction of findings meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic granularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographic granularity where relevant / geographic comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide geographic breakdowns or maps when geography matters; granular location information increases local newsroom pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample/scope clearly stated
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample/scope clearly stated / sample size disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state sample size, population, sampling method, and scope so journalists can assess representativeness and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence and uncertainty disclosed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report confidence intervals, margins of error, or other measures of uncertainty rather than presenting point estimates as absolute facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline with specific number
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A headline that includes a specific numeric top-line finding makes the release immediately newsworthy and quotable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead with most striking finding
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put the key finding up front in the lead paragraph so busy editors and reporters see the news hook immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date range provided
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the temporal scope of the data (e.g., dates covered) so readers understand recency and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author/researcher identified and available
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List the researcher/author and provide contact details; offering an expert for comment increases pickup likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding source disclosed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare funding and conflicts of interest to allow journalists to assess potential biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topline chart (one big finding)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a single clear headline chart that communicates the main result at a glance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed data tables
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide tables for reporters and data journalists who want to see the underlying numbers or perform secondary analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic visualization
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maps or geographically tagged charts help localize stories and increase appeal to regional outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology infographic
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A visual summary of methods helps non-technical journalists grasp study design quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embeddable visualizations/widgets
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide embeddable HTML/iframes or widgets so digital outlets can drop visuals directly into their pages; embeddables increase reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Static images for traditional media
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include high-resolution PNG/JPG charts for print and broadcast use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive visualizations for digital
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer interactive charts/filters for online outlets and data journalists who want drill‑down capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data file available for re-analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Data file (CSV) available for data journalists to remix / data file available for re-analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide downloadable machine-readable data (CSV/Excel) so reporters and analysts can reproduce and extend findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple pre-bundled story angles
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple story angles pre-identified / pre-bundled story angles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply several ready-made angles (top-line, demographic breakdowns, geographic comparisons, trend over time, surprising sub-findings) to increase the chance a journalist finds a usable hook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demographic breakdowns
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disaggregate results by relevant demographics (age, gender, income, ethnicity) to enable audience-targeted stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trend over time
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show changes across time to give context on trajectory rather than only cross-sectional snapshots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprising sub-findings highlighted
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag counterintuitive or newsworthy subgroup results that could serve as alternate hooks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology document linked
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a link to the complete methods/report for journalists who need technical detail or wish to verify procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations acknowledged
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State study limitations openly (sampling limitations, measurement error, generalizability) to build trust and prevent misinterpretation.
